summary: Iteration 5 testing — all 5 new features verified end-to-end (backend + frontend). BACKEND: added /app/backend/tests/test_iteration5.py (17 tests, 100% pass). Full regression `pytest tests -n 0` = 147/147 passing (iter2 39 + iter3 44 + iter4 47 + iter5 17). Leaderboard endpoint behaves per spec: STAFF-only (OWNER 200, ACCOUNTANT 200, FIELD_AGENT 403, no-org 403, bad-token 401); default month resolves to current (2026-10); invalid months (not-a-month, 2025-13, abcd-01, 2025/01, 2025-1a) all 400; every agent row carries user_id/name/email/rank/sales_total/sales_count/customers_count/collections_total/returns_total; rank is 1-based and sorted by sales_total DESC; a historical empty month (2000-01) returns zeros for every agent; voided sales are excluded (created a sale total=40, leaderboard sales_total +40 and sales_count +1, voided via /sales/{id}/void, leaderboard dropped exactly 40 and sales_count returned to pre-sale value). (5) STATEMENT PDF (accountant tab-customers > row): statement-sheet opens with statement-share-pdf-button, statement-print-button and statement-whatsapp-button all present. REGRESSION: accountant still has all 5 bottom tabs (tab-index / tab-sales / tab-collections / tab-debts / tab-customers); list-search-input, list-summary-total, list-summary-count still render on the sales list. No React Native red screens, no pageerrors, no HTTP 4xx/5xx during the UI run. The 'props.pointerEvents is deprecated' third-party warning tracked from iter4 is still present (non-blocking).

(Nice-to-have) Add an API-level test asserting that a sale created in month N does NOT appear when leaderboard is requested with month N-1 (cross-month boundary). Current coverage asserts the empty-month path (2000-01) and current-month inclusion/exclusion; explicit month-boundary test would make the YYYY-MM filter airtight.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py agents_leaderboard: filters sales by {'created_at': rng} where rng uses date-string bounds (YYYY-MM-DD). Since sales.created_at is ISO datetime (iso()) a string lexicographic compare works correctly here, but this is implicit — a brief comment or using proper datetime objects would make the intent and correctness obvious.

server.py now ~1700 lines; splitting routes into submodules (deliveries, sales, stats, admin, routes-planner) is overdue — iter5 added leaderboard inline alongside overview/agents/reports which is fine but makes server.py the single-biggest refactor target.

Leaderboard currently iterates agents and issues N+2 queries per agent (sales find + 2 _sum aggregations). For orgs with >100 agents this is O(3N) round-trips. A single $facet aggregation keyed by distributor_id would scale better. Not blocking (seed has 1 agent, orgs rarely >10).

rca_of_issue: No bugs found. Both backend endpoint and all five frontend features behave exactly to spec. The only latent note is that /api/stats/leaderboard uses a date-string range filter against ISO datetime strings — this works because ISO datetime strings are lexicographically ordered the same as datetimes with the same prefix, but using datetime objects would be clearer; non-blocking.
